projectTitle: Expelliodor — Expel the Odor, on Your Terms
tagline: Three de novo designed proteins that stop axillary odour before it forms, without killing the skin microbiome.
summary: Axillary odour arises when Staphylococcus hominis imports the odourless precursor Cys-Gly-3M3SH through the peptide transporter PepTSh and converts it to 3M3SH. Rather than killing skin bacteria, GreatBay-SCIE attacked the uptake step three ways: a de novo small-molecule binding protein that sequesters the precursor, a de novo protein binder designed to lock PepTSh in its inward-facing conformation, and a cyclodextrin glucanotransferase engineered to glycosylate the precursor so the transporter no longer recognises it. This is the most sophisticated de novo protein design campaign of any high school team in the cohort — RFdiffusion3, Proteina-Complexa, ProteinMPNN, RoseTTAFold3 co-folding, 50-ns MD with MM/GBSA, and SPURS-guided thermostability engineering — organised around two frameworks they invented: a Characterize stage prepended to DBTL, and a funnel-shaped decision-gated workflow that spends expensive methods only on candidates that survive cheap ones. Nine precursor binders and five transporter binders were actually tested in vitro, with 4 of 9 and 4 of 5 significantly reducing 3M3SH.
awards: Best Integrated Human Practices nominee (High School)

dry.frameworks: Two methodological contributions frame everything. The CHARACTERIZE-DBTL framework inserts a stage before Design with four substages — Problem Definition (what the design must achieve, in what context, with what intervention points), Target Definition (the exact molecule, protein, conformational state, interface or reaction to engineer, with boundaries), Mechanistic Characterization (assess the plausibility of the proposed mechanism against experimental, structural and computational evidence), and Design Specification (translate all of that into explicit requirements that become the literal inputs to the design tool). The DECISION-GATED WORKFLOW is a funnel in which each successive evaluation is more expensive than the last, so a large generated set is cut by cheap co-folding metrics before anything reaches molecular dynamics and only a handful reach the bench — explicitly chosen because they are a high school team with limited wet-lab resources. The Characterize stage paid off concretely in each of the three routes. For the PRECURSOR BINDER, characterisation established that 3M3SH exists as two stereoisomers with different smells, that the sweat-and-onion-like (S) form is the odour-relevant one, and that deep-learning design tools frequently introduce stereochemical errors — so the design specification became 'use Cys-Gly-(S)-3M3SH with explicitly defined stereochemistry as input and verify ligand chirality after structure generation before any candidate advances'. Two independent design routes were run in parallel for comparison: RFdiffusion3 (via Rosetta Foundry, with ProteinMPNN sequence redesign and RoseTTAFold3 co-folding validation, ranked by RF3's own ranking_score) and Proteina-Complexa (a partially-latent flow-matching model, ranked by a custom composite score). Top binders from each route went to 50-ns MD scored on ligand RMSD and MM/GBSA binding free energy. For the TRANSPORTER BINDER, characterisation drew on published MD showing that the inward-to-outward transition is the rate-limiting step of PepTSh's transport cycle, so stabilising the inward-facing state should block transport; they took the experimental inward-facing crystal structure (PDB 6EXS), built an outward-facing homology model in SWISS-MODEL, and compared them to find extracellular electrostatic networks (K64-E323, and the R184/D182/E340/R337 cluster) and hydrophobic patches present only in the inward-facing state — those became the target interface, with a specification of an 80-120 residue binder and a preference for compact designs to improve accessibility through a Gram-positive cell wall. Design was RFdiffusion3 backbone generation, ProteinMPNN sequence design, RF3 co-folding, interface-placement filtering, then a composite score of 0.50 x normalised ranking score + 0.25 x normalised pLDDT + 0.25 x normalised inverse PAE, then MD. For CGTase, characterisation enumerated the three modifiable groups on the precursor (amino, carboxyl, hydroxyl) and selected reactions by compatibility with the actual application environment — mildly acidic human skin with no external supply of ATP or NADH — which ruled out cofactor-dependent chemistry and left hydroxyl transglycosylation by CGTase; molecular docking from the 1CXL template with cluster analysis of poses, followed by MD of the wild-type complex, showed the non-native substrate stays stably accommodated in the catalytic pocket and identified which interactions were weak (around the carboxylate group and the hydrophobic tail), which became the rational-design targets for nine point mutants, each re-evaluated by MD. Two further optimisation campaigns followed: CGTase thermostability via SPURS (an AI stability predictor) after excluding conserved, ligand-binding and calcium-coordinating residues, with FireProt-style pairwise compatibility filtering and a diversity-preserving beam search assembling multi-point mutants at depths of 2, 4, 6 and 8 substitutions; and precursor-binder affinity via an adapted LASErMPNN neural-proofreading strategy, saturating point mutations within 5 Angstrom of the ligand, averaging probabilities across decoding orders and dropout to reduce sensitivity to individual predictions, ranking by delta-NLL = ln[P(a)/P(b)], and filtering out buried polar residues introduced without a suitable hydrogen bond.
dry.dataviz: Structural figures are used as arguments rather than decoration. The inward- versus outward-facing PepTSh comparison is drawn as four aligned panels — the inward structure, a close-up of its intact electrostatic network with dashed contacts and named residues, the outward homology model, and the same close-up showing those contacts broken — so the reader can see for themselves why the inward state is the one worth stabilising, with consistent colouring (green C-terminal bundle, blue N-terminal bundle, orange TMA/TMB) carried across every panel. The target interface is then shown three ways: the region highlighted on the whole structure, a side view with the extracellular direction arrowed, and a close-up with hotspot residues in orange bordering a green hydrophobic patch. The Characterize stage and the funnel-shaped decision-gated workflow are each drawn as schematics, the funnel visibly narrowing through each evaluation gate. MD trajectories are embedded as videos for all three systems. Most valuable of all, Figures 7 and 11 plot computational metric against experimental outcome — A412 signal reduction, calculated as 100 x (1 - mean binder A412 / mean control A412) — with each tested binder as a point, OLS regression lines, and both Pearson r and Spearman rho reported, separately for the two design routes. Every caption gives the n (n = 4 for RFdiffusion3, n = 5 for Proteina-Complexa and for transporter binders) and the full composite-score formula with its weights written out, so the figure can be re-derived. Assay figures carry error bars (+/- SD, n = 3) with significance asterisks defined.
dry.datascience: The genuinely unusual thing here is that the team treat their own scoring metrics as hypotheses to be tested against wet-lab data, and publish the result honestly even when it undermines them. Of 22 planned binders (11 per design tool), 9 were tested; 4 of 9 significantly reduced 3M3SH production, and 4 of 5 transporter binders did, with a maximum 21% reduction. Correlating metric against outcome gave a route-dependent answer: in the RFdiffusion3 branch the interface metrics agreed with experiment and all three MD metrics (MM/GBSA delta-G, and the mean and SD of ligand RMSD over 10-50 ns) showed the expected trend, while in the Proteina-Complexa branch the custom composite score correlated best (Pearson r = 0.76, Spearman rho = 0.60) but the MD metrics did NOT agree — and the team propose a specific mechanistic reason, that RF3 (a diffusion model, like RoseTTAFold3) may predict Proteina-Complexa outputs (partially latent flow matching) less accurately, so ligand RMSD may partly measure relaxation of a poor predicted pose rather than true instability. For the transporter binders they draw the sharper statistical lesson: 'in a filtered set of candidates, a single metric may have too little variation to support confident prediction of actual experimental performance' — i.e. gating on a metric destroys the variance you would need to validate it. They state plainly that the small candidate set 'cannot establish statistically significant relationships', that the results 'cannot concretely verify the usefulness of the single metrics and the weighted metrics we set', and they name the fixes: more independent MD runs, explicit entropy correction, an implicit membrane model in the free-energy calculation, a second folding tool such as AlphaFold, and larger datasets to recalibrate weights. The thermostability work produced a real, interpretable result in both directions: for the T370R/F183W parent, WR2, WR4 and WR8 all improved over the parent with WR8 best, suggesting SPURS (trained on pairwise mutagenesis data) can learn patterns that extrapolate to multi-point mutants and that the design introduced beneficial epistasis; but for the T370K parent only KR2 improved and the higher-order mutants did not, which the team diagnose as the beam search's path dependence — an ineffective mutation introduced at depth 4 is inherited by every deeper mutant. They are equally candid about build failures: the intended T370K mutant came back as T370L, so only T370R/F183W was tested as designed and the rational-design hypothesis is 'not fully verified because of the limited dataset'.
dry.software: FoundryUI, a node-based visual programming workbench for de novo protein design, explicitly inspired by ComfyUI (and by Blender and GameMaker as precedents for making technical workflows accessible). It wraps four Rosetta Foundry tools — RFdiffusion3, RoseTTAFold3, ProteinMPNN and LigandMPNN — as connectable nodes for input, generation, sequence redesign, folding, filtering, visualisation and saving, with typed connections that refuse incompatible links, 3D selectors so residues and atoms can be picked directly off a structure in the GUI rather than typed as indices, and sessions and runs so results survive a dropped connection. It ships pre-built workflows for ligand-binder design, protein-binder design, enzyme design, MPNN sequence design and folding prediction, and reads and writes PDB, FASTA, mmCIF, SMILES, JSON and CSV so outputs stay usable elsewhere. The stated motivation is collaboration as much as accessibility: a command line does not show why a step was chosen or how data moved between stages, whereas a graph does — making a workflow easier to explain, modify and hand to the next team. They tested it by teaching it: FoundryUI was used in a school club education activity so students could approach protein modelling through biological decisions instead of commands. All automation scripts are uploaded as reusable workflows for future iGEM teams.
techniques: conformational-state-selective targeting (inward vs outward transporter state)
homology modelling for comparative structure analysis
interface hotspot and hydrophobic patch identification
molecular docking with hierarchical pose clustering
diverse beam search for multi-point mutant assembly
neural proofreading with delta-NLL ranking and decoding-order averaging
composite multi-metric scoring with explicit weights
Ellman's assay quantification of thiol product

good.publicEngagement: Inclusivity Award winner, and the work is built on a framework (LIFT+: Learn, Intervene, Feedback, Transfer, Beyond) with six named target groups reachable in China who face barriers to synthetic biology — the blind community, the Deaf community, children on the autism spectrum, people from low socioeconomic backgrounds, modelling beginners, and older adults with limited formal education. Each group is introduced by a real scientist from that community paired with a sourced statistic: Wanda Diaz Merced, the blind astrophysicist who pioneered sonification of astronomical data, alongside the finding that only 2.1% of blind children globally have access to specialised education services; Temple Grandin alongside the 14.95% four-year-college enrolment rate for individuals with autism; Derek Braun, the deaf geneticist who built Gallaudet's first molecular genetics laboratory, alongside the ~80% of school-age deaf children out of school in low- and middle-income countries; Gabriel Reyes, founder of FLi Sci, alongside OECD data that 37% of disadvantaged students are low performers in science versus 12% of advantaged; and Jia Lanpo, the Zhoukoudian paleoanthropologist who had only a high school education, alongside the 17-point generational gap in tertiary education between adults aged 55-64 and 25-34. Deliverables include 20 tactile biology graphics covering 20 topics across 5 categories for the blind community, and — connecting directly to their dry lab — FoundryUI used as the teaching vehicle for computational protein design beginners. The page itself has an interactive animated version and a text-based alternative, which is the inclusivity principle applied to their own wiki.
good.ihp: 46 stakeholder interactions across local and international surveys, potential-customer interviews, expert discussions, industry meetings, written proposals and community seminars, organised into a five-stage framework with stakeholders classified into four groups by how they affect the team and how the team affects them, plus a closing 'Feedback to Future' section that explains how they decided which feedback to prioritise and revisited stakeholders to reflect. The clearest evidence that the integration was real is that it changed the project's own name: they started with 'Expelliodor — Expel the Odor', then, prompted by social scientists on stigma, asked whether 'expel' implied that odour is something everyone should eliminate, and why axillary odour should be judged differently from hair or eye colour. They concluded that underarm odour is a natural physiological trait rather than a flaw to be corrected and that managing it should be a matter of choice, and changed the slogan to 'Expel the Odor, on Your Terms' — keeping the scientific goal while adding personal autonomy. Medical experts pushed safety, industry professionals pushed real-world feasibility, and the whole design philosophy of not broadly suppressing skin bacteria or blocking sweat glands follows from that engagement.
good.realWorld: The entrepreneurship case is grounded in population genetics rather than vague market size: the ABCC11 odour-associated allele occurs at roughly 99.99% in African, 97.48% in European, 96.05% in Oceanian, 92.42% in American, 62.22% in Southern Asian and 21.54% in Eastern Asian populations, so even in East Asia where it is least common the absolute population means tens of millions may be affected — and limited public awareness compounds misunderstanding, stigma and discrimination. The team position Expelliodor against the actual failure modes of existing products (masking fragrances, aluminium-salt antiperspirants that suppress perspiration, and broad antibacterials that disturb the axillary microbiome) and argue their three strategies are complementary in time: the precursor binder captures what is already there, CGTase continuously modifies newly secreted precursor, and the transporter binder blocks uptake. CGTase thermostability optimisation was undertaken specifically for industrial production and transportation, which is why heat resistance during storage was a design objective at all.

images.caption: The funnel-shaped decision-gated workflow: successive evaluation gates remove designs from a large generated space until a small testing set remains, with each gate more computationally expensive than the last. Designed explicitly so a high school team with limited wet-lab resources spends molecular dynamics time only on candidates that already survived cheap co-folding filters.

Four RFdiffusion3 precursor binders plotted as computational metric against measured A412 signal reduction, with MM/GBSA binding free energy and both the mean and the standard deviation of MD ligand RMSD over 10-50 ns. All three MD metrics showed the expected trend in this branch — while the same metrics failed in the Proteina-Complexa branch, which the team report and explain rather than omit.

Close-up of the inward-facing PepTSh transporter (PDB 6EXS) showing the extracellular electrostatic network as dashed contacts linking K64 to E323 and connecting R184, D182, E340 and R337. Comparing this against the same region in an outward-facing homology model, where those contacts are broken, is what defined the binder's target interface.

The selected target interface on the extracellular surface of PepTSh: orange hotspot residues bordering a green hydrophobic patch on the blue extracellular face. These features exist only in the inward-facing conformation, so a binder that holds them is designed to block the inward-to-outward transition that published molecular dynamics identified as the rate-limiting step of transport.

gemsTakeaway: Add a Characterize stage before Design: write down the biological mechanism, the exact target and the application environment, and turn them into an explicit design specification that becomes the literal input to your tool — GreatBay's specification to use the (S) stereoisomer and verify chirality after generation prevented a whole class of silent AI-design error. Then plot every computational score you used against the wet-lab outcome and report the correlation, including the honest finding that gating on a metric removes the variance you would need to validate it.
